*{{Rarity|Rare}} cards have 14 different Levels, ranging from Level 3 to Level 16.
*{{Rarity|Epic}} cards have 11 different Levels, ranging from Level 6 to Level 16.
*{{Rarity|Legendary}} cards have 8 different Levels, ranging from Level 9 to Level 16.
*{{Rarity|Champion}} cards have 6 different Levels, ranging from Level 11 to Level 16.
sources.note: Internally consistent: cap 16 minus floor plus 1 equals the stated level count for every rarity. History section (same revid) dates the floors to the 5/9/2018 level renumbering (Rare 3 / Epic 6 / Legendary 9) and the 27/10/2021 Champions update (Champion floor 11 = new Tournament Standard); 24/11/2025 update raised the cap to 16 without touching floors.
Checked and ruled out as a floor source: this page is player/King Level XP, not card levels. The floor table lives on Cards.
Champion floor applied to the statistics table; see mighty_miner_check.

mighty_miner_check.editor_comment_verbatim: ONLY change the numbers in the three variables directly below (hp_lvl1, dmg_lvl1, atk_speed), THAT WILL BE LEVEL 11.

explosive_escape_ladder_game_model.method: levels.py percent-table model: base_for(332 @ L11) = 130 (unique inversion, floor(130*2.56)=332); at_level(130, L) = floor(130*PERCENT[L]/100)

440_441.detail: at_level(130,14) = floor(130*3.39) = 440 — the ONLY level in 1..19 producing 440 or 441. Wiki's 1.1^n rendering gives 442 at L14 (exact 441.892); the 2-point gap is the wiki's known 1.1^n-vs-percent-table drift, not a level ambiguity. Neighbours L13=401/402 and L15=483/486 are far away.

366.detail: No level in 1..19 produces 366 under either model (wiki L12 = 365, game L12 = 365). 366 is the L12 exact value 365.2 rounded UP (ceil) instead of round-half-up, or an equivalently mis-anchored derivation. Any pipeline emitting 366 is not reading a published or game value.

impact_on_other_rarities.L11_vardefine_interpretation: UNCHANGED for every rarity. Measured: all 78 archived card pages anchor every leveled stat vardefine at the absolute suffix _11 (47x hp_11, 47x dmg_11, plus escape_11, death_11, etc.); zero pages anchor at 1, 3, 6, 9, or 13. The vardefine name carries the absolute level, so rarity floors cannot shift what an L11 vardefine means — floor-anchoring changes no stored KB reference value.
where_floors_DO_matter: Reverse-deriving a level from an in-game observation: the candidate level set must be clamped to [floor, 16] for the card's rarity. For Champions only 6 published rows exist (11-16); an inferred level below the rarity floor is impossible and signals a mis-anchored derivation (the 366 case).

levels.py base_for() inversion to L1: for Rare/Epic/Legendary/Champion the L1 base is fictional in gameplay terms (no such card can exist below its floor) but is exactly the game's internal storage model (level-1 stat + shared percent table), so the arithmetic stays valid. The caveat is interpretive: never treat the inverted L1 base as an observable stat, and never query at_level() below the rarity floor when validating against real matches.
Breakpoint tables built per level: rows below a rarity's floor describe matchups that cannot occur on ladder and must be excluded rather than trained on.

levels_py.note: Both copies byte-identical (diff clean). REF_LEVEL=11, PERCENT[11]=256, MAX_LEVEL=19.
